system.name: Store
system.description: Step 2: the first consumer and the provider, at Level 1 only. Cut from the walkthrough's full map of the Store. An online store that sells home goods to shoppers through a web shop and a mobile app, with internal tools for its fraud analysts and store managers.

corpus.included: Nothing real: the Store is an invented example, written by hand to teach the boundary model. No repository exists. The places and evidence name invented folders and files.
corpus.excluded: Shopper sign-in and accounts, saved cards and delivery addresses, which a real store would have. They are left out to keep the example small.

consumers.name: Shopper
consumers.description: A person who buys home goods from the Store, on the web or in the mobile app.

providers.name: Store
providers.description: The online store as its shoppers and staff know it: the web shop, the mobile app and the staff tools.

parts.name: Web shop and mobile app clients
parts.why: They present the Store's capabilities to shoppers and keep nothing of their own, so they are parts of the web shop and mobile app interfaces.

parts.name: Mobile gateway
parts.why: It passes the mobile app's calls on to the components and trims the answers for small screens. It keeps nothing and decides nothing, so it is part of the mobile app interface.

parts.name: Dashboard, review console and store CLI
parts.why: Clients for staff, parts of their interfaces. The store CLI's database commands work on the system, so they are listed in excluded.

parts.name: Money library
parts.why: Rounds amounts and formats prices for every component. A library, not a component.

resources.name: Product
resources.description: Something the Store sells, with its price and its stock. A product can be on many orders.

resources.name: Order
resources.description: A shopper's purchase of one or more products. Each order belongs to one shopper.
properties: status: placed, on hold, confirmed, shipped, delivered or canceled

resources.name: Loyalty balance
resources.description: The points a shopper has earned from orders. Each shopper has one.
properties: points that expire next, and when

interfaces.name: web shop
interfaces.description: The Store's website, where shoppers browse, order, and follow and cancel their orders.

interfaces.name: mobile app
interfaces.description: The Store's phone app. It offers what the web shop offers, and uses the phone's camera to show a product in the shopper's room.

areas.name: Shop
areas.description: Find products, buy them, and follow or cancel what was bought.

capabilities.name: Browse products
capabilities.gives: the matching products, with their prices and whether they are in stock

capabilities.name: Place order
capabilities.takes: a cart, a delivery address and a card
capabilities.gives: the order, confirmed or on hold for review, with the points it earned; or a declined card to try again

capabilities.name: List past orders
capabilities.gives: the shopper's orders, with their status, total and tracking number

capabilities.name: Cancel order
capabilities.takes: an order that has not shipped yet
capabilities.gives: the order canceled, its money refunded to the card, and its points taken back

areas.name: See product in your room
areas.description: See how a product would look, at its real size, in a room at home.

capabilities.name: See product in your room
capabilities.takes: a product, and the phone's camera pointed at a room
capabilities.gives: the product drawn at its real size in the camera's view of the room

areas.name: See loyalty balance
areas.description: See the points earned from past orders.

capabilities.name: See loyalty balance
capabilities.gives: the points balance, and the points that expire next

evidence.shows: the checkout, where a shopper places an order and tries another card after a decline
past orders, with a cancel button on orders that have not shipped
the camera view that draws a product in a room, which the web shop does not have

cleanupCandidates.name: Old checkout
cleanupCandidates.why: apps/web-shop/src/legacy-checkout is the checkout the web shop used before the current one. A flag still turns it on, but no shopper reaches it.

excluded.name: Database commands of the store CLI
excluded.why: `store migrate` and `store seed` change the database schema and load test data. They work on the system, not with it.

excluded.name: Fraud model training
excluded.why: ml/fraud-model trains the model Fraud check scores with. It changes how the system decides, so it works on the system.

excluded.name: Deploy and infrastructure
excluded.why: infra/ and the CI workflows build and ship the Store.

excluded.name: Flagging risky payments
excluded.why: Fraud check flags payments on its own, as part of scoring them. No consumer asks for it: analysts review what it flagged.

excluded.name: Points expiry
excluded.why: Storefront expires points a year after they are earned, on its own. Shoppers see the points that expire next on their balance.

excluded.name: Search index rebuild and health checks
excluded.why: Machinery that keeps browsing fast and the services up. Nobody uses it for a purpose of their own.
